celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿إِذَا وَقَعَتِ الْوَاقِعَةُ﴾ when the Resurrection takes place,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ﴾ a soul that denies it by negating it, as it negated it in this world;

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿خَافِضَةٌ رَافِعَةٌ﴾ that is, manifesting the lowering of some peoples by their entering the Fire, and the raising of others by their entering Paradise;

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِذَا رُجَّتِ الْأَرْضُ رَجًّا﴾ is shaken violently,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿فَكَانَتْ هَبَاءً﴾ dust ﴿مُنْبَثًّا﴾ scattered — and the second إِذَا is a badal (substitute) for the first —

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَأَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾ — they are those who are given their books in their right hands — a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿مَا أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ﴾ a magnification of their standing through their entering Paradise;

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَأَصْحَابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ﴾ of the left, in that each of them is given his book in his left hand: ﴿مَا أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ﴾ a belittling of their standing through their entering the Fire;

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَالسَّابِقُونَ﴾ to good — and they are the prophets — a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿السَّابِقُونَ﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) to magnify their standing; and the khabar (predicate) is:

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, a large group of the past nations,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ﴾ of the community of Muhammad ﷺ; and they are the foremost of the past nations and of this community; and the khabar (predicate) is:

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿عَلَى سُرُرٍ مَوْضُونَةٍ﴾ woven with rods of gold and jewels,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْهَا مُتَقَابِلِينَ﴾ two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the pronoun in the khabar (predicate).

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ in service ﴿وِلْدَانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ in the form of boys, never growing old,

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿بِأَكْوَابٍ﴾ cups without handles ﴿وَأَبَارِيقَ﴾ which have handles and spouts, ﴿وَكَأْسٍ﴾ a vessel for drinking wine ﴿مِنْ مَعِينٍ﴾ that is, wine flowing from a spring that never ceases,

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿لَا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْهَا وَلَا يُنْزَفُونَ﴾ with fatḥa and kasra on the zāy [يُنْزِفُونَ], from نَزَفَ الشَّارِبُ and أَنْزَفَ, that is, no headache results for them from it nor loss of mind, unlike the wine of this world;

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَفَاكِهَةٍ مِمَّا يَتَخَيَّرُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَلَحْمِ طَيْرٍ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَ﴾ for them, for enjoyment, are ﴿حُورٌ﴾ women with intensely black and white eyes, ﴿عِينٌ﴾ large-eyed; its ʿayn has kasra instead of ḍamma for harmony with the yāʾ, and its singular is عَيْنَاءُ, like حَمْرَاءَ; and in one reading حُورٍ عِينٍ are in the genitive,

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿جَزَاءً﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) or a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the governing word (ʿāmil) is implied, that is: We have made what is mentioned for them as a recompense, or: We have recompensed them; ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿لَا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا﴾ in Paradise ﴿لَغْوًا﴾ obscene speech ﴿وَلَا تَأْثِيمًا﴾ what leads to sin,

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ (meaning: but) ﴿قِيلًا﴾ a saying: ﴿سَلَامًا سَلَامًا﴾ a badal (substitute) for قِيلًا; for they do hear it.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَأَصْحَابُ الْيَمِينِ مَا أَصْحَابُ الْيَمِينِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَطَلْحٍ﴾ banana trees ﴿مَنْضُودٍ﴾ layered with fruit from bottom to top,

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَفَاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿لَا مَقْطُوعَةٍ﴾ at any time ﴿وَلَا مَمْنُوعَةٍ﴾ for a price,

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْشَأْنَاهُنَّ إِنْشَاءً﴾ that is, the ḥūr ʿīn, without birth,

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُنَّ أَبْكَارًا﴾ virgins: whenever their husbands come to them they find them virgins, and without pain;

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿عُرُبًا﴾ with ḍamma and sukūn on the rāʾ, plural of عَرُوبٍ, the one who endears herself to her husband out of passionate love for him; ﴿أَتْرَابًا﴾ plural of تِرْبٍ, that is, equal in age,

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿لِأَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ connected (ṣila) to أَنْشَأْنَاهُنَّ or جَعَلْنَاهُنَّ; they are

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَأَصْحَابُ الشِّمَالِ مَا أَصْحَابُ الشِّمَالِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿فِي سَمُومٍ﴾ a hot wind from the Fire that penetrates the pores ﴿وَحَمِيمٍ﴾ water of intense heat,

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿لَا بَارِدٍ﴾ like other shades ﴿وَلَا كَرِيمٍ﴾ pleasant to look at.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ﴾ in this world ﴿مُتْرَفِينَ﴾ living in ease, not toiling in obedience,

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَكَانُوا يُصِرُّونَ عَلَى الْحِنْثِ﴾ the sin ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ that is, idolatry (shirk),

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَكَانُوا يَقُولُونَ أَئِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا وَعِظَامًا أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ In the two hamzas, in both places, there is full pronunciation (taḥqīq), softening (tashīl) of the second, and the insertion of an alif between them, in both ways.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿أَوْ آبَاؤُنَا الْأَوَّلُونَ﴾ with fatḥa on the wāw, for conjunction, and the hamza for interrogation; and in this and what precedes it, it is for expressing improbability. And in one reading the wāw has sukūn, conjoining with أَوْ, and what it is conjoined to is the position (maḥall) of إِنَّ and its noun.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿لَمَجْمُوعُونَ إِلَى مِيقَاتِ﴾ for the time of ﴿يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ﴾ that is, the Day of Resurrection.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ أَيُّهَا الضَّالُّونَ الْمُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿لَآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ﴾ an explanation (bayān) of الشَّجَر,

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿فَشَارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ that is, on the zaqqūm eaten, ﴿مِنَ الْحَمِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿فَشَارِبُونَ شَرْبَ﴾ with fatḥa and ḍamma on the shīn, a maṣdar (verbal noun) [شُرْبَ], ﴿الْهِيمِ﴾ thirsty camels; plural of هَيْمَانَ for the male and هَيْمَى for the female, like عَطْشَانَ and عَطْشَى.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿هَذَا نُزُلُهُمْ﴾ what is prepared for them ﴿يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾ on the Day of Resurrection.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ We brought you into being from non-existence; ﴿فَلَوْلَا﴾ why then not ﴿تُصَدِّقُونَ﴾ the resurrection? For the One able to originate is able to restore.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ مَا تُمْنُونَ﴾ the semen you pour into the wombs of women:

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second changed into an alif, and softened, and with an alif inserted between the softened one and the other, and without it, in the four places; ﴿تَخْلُقُونَهُ﴾ that is, the semen, into a human being, ﴿أَمْ نَحْنُ الْخَالِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنَا﴾ with the doubled and the light [dāl] ﴿بَيْنَكُمُ الْمَوْتَ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ unable

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿عَلَى﴾ (meaning: to) ﴿أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ﴾ put ﴿أَمْثَالَكُمْ﴾ in your place ﴿وَنُنْشِئَكُمْ﴾ create you ﴿فِي مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ of forms, such as apes and swine.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ النَّشَأَةَ الْأُولَى﴾ — and in one reading with sukūn on the shīn [النَّشْأَةَ] — ﴿فَلَوْلَا تَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ in it there is assimilation of the second tāʾ of the original form into the dhāl [تَذَكَّرُونَ].

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ مَا تَحْرُثُونَ﴾ you stir up the soil and cast the seed into it:

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ﴾ make it grow, ﴿أَمْ نَحْنُ الزَّارِعُونَ﴾

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿لَوْ نَشَاءُ لَجَعَلْنَاهُ حُطَامًا﴾ dry plants with no grain in them, ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ﴾ its original form is ظَلِلْتُمْ with kasra on the lām, which was omitted for lightness, that is, you would remain all day ﴿تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾ one of the two tāʾs of the original form was omitted from it; marvelling at that and saying:

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ﴾ the cost of our crops,

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ﴾ deprived of our provision.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ الْمَاءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ أَنْزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ الْمُزْنِ﴾ the clouds, plural of مُزْنَةٍ, ﴿أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿لَوْ نَشَاءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجًا﴾ salty, impossible to drink; ﴿فَلَوْلَا﴾ why then not ﴿تَشْكُرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ﴾ you bring out from green trees:

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ أَنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَهَا﴾ such as markh, ʿafār and kalkh, ﴿أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْشِئُونَ﴾

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿نَحْنُ جَعَلْنَاهَا تَذْكِرَةً﴾ of the fire of Hell ﴿وَمَتَاعًا﴾ a means of subsistence ﴿لِلْمُقْوِينَ﴾ for travellers; from أَقْوَى الْقَوْمُ, that is, they came to be in al-qawā — with the short and the long vowel — that is, the wilderness, which is a desert with no plants or water in it.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ﴾ declare transcendent ﴿بِاسْمِ﴾ redundant (zāʾid) ﴿رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ that is, Allah.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿فَلَا أُقْسِمُ﴾ لَا is redundant (zāʾida); ﴿بِمَوَاقِعِ النُّجُومِ﴾ their falling places as they set;

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ that is, the oath by them, ﴿لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ﴾ that is, if you were people of knowledge you would know the greatness of this oath.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ that is, what is recited to you, ﴿لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿فِي كِتَابٍ﴾ written, ﴿مَكْنُونٍ﴾ guarded; and it is the Muṣḥaf.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿لَا يَمَسُّهُ﴾ a statement (khabar) in the sense of a prohibition, ﴿إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ that is, those who have purified themselves of ritual impurities (aḥdāth).

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿أَفَبِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ﴾ the Quran ﴿أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ﴾ taking it lightly and denying it,

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ﴾ of rain, that is, gratitude for it, ﴿أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ Allah's giving of water, in that you said: "We were given rain by such-and-such a star (nawʾ)."

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿فَلَوْلَا﴾ why then not, ﴿إِذَا بَلَغَتِ﴾ the soul, at the time of the death-throes, ﴿الْحُلْقُومَ﴾ it is the passage of food,

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ﴾ O you present with the dying person ﴿حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ at him,

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ﴾ in knowledge, ﴿وَلَكِنْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ from baṣīra (insight), that is, you do not know that;

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿فَلَوْلَا﴾ why then not, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ﴾ recompensed by being resurrected, that is, not to be resurrected, as you claim,

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿تَرْجِعُونَهَا﴾ return the soul to the body after it has reached the throat, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in what you claim? The second فَلَوْلَا is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first; and إِذَا is an adverb (ẓarf) for تَرْجِعُونَ, to which the two conditions are attached. The meaning is: why do you not return it, if you deny the resurrection and are truthful in denying it? That is, so that death would be negated from its place, like the resurrection.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ﴾ the dead person ﴿مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿فَرَوْحٌ﴾ that is, for him there is rest, ﴿وَرَيْحَانٌ﴾ goodly provision, ﴿وَجَنَّتُ نَعِيمٍ﴾. Whether the apodosis (jawāb) belongs to أَمَّا or to أَنْ [Translator's note: the source writes لأن; the conditional إِنْ is meant], or to both, there are [several] views.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿فَسَلَامٌ لَكَ﴾ that is, for him is safety from punishment, ﴿مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ by virtue of his being one of them.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ الضَّالِّينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾ of the type of annexing the qualified noun to its adjective.

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ This has been explained before.
